title: Middle Man / Excessive Delegation
pattern: A class or struct whose entire public API or a vast majority of methods consist of delegating calls to another helper class without performing any domain logic of its own.
why_bad: It introduces unnecessary indirection and boilerplate. Over-encapsulation results in a class that serves as an empty shell, obscuring the actual flow of control and making the execution path hard to trace.
detection: A struct where most methods (e.g., greater than 80%) do nothing but forward their arguments and return values directly to an internal field object without transformation.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. A facade pattern designed to group and simplify access to a complex, multi-object subsystem, or a proxy/decorator adding dynamic concerns (e.g. logging/security).
fix: Eliminate the middle man using the Remove Middle Man refactoring: let the caller access the underlying delegated objects directly.
source: Martin Fowler et al., *Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code* (1999), Chapter 3 ("Bad Smells in Code - Middle Man"), pp. 110, 259–260; Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 24.
